os_version: Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12.95+deb13-amd64, headless server — Xvfb (X11), no WM
app: Native OS-level blind click driven by structured coordinates — completed on three stacks (was: partial/blocked in the old sandbox)

stack_detection.method: open debug port / AT-SPI bus registration
stack_detection.signature: CDP :9223 responds; apps registered on org.a11y bus

channel_setup: The 2026-08-14 sandbox cell recorded this path 'blocked' after Chromium's DevTools port stopped binding across relaunches. On this machine the same script ran first try. Three independent end-to-end runs, all with REAL OS clicks (xdotool/XTEST — the input path an OS agent would use), never a synthetic in-channel click: (a) Chromium/CDP via campaign/linux/blind-click-linux.mjs (identical logic to campaign/desktop/blind_click.mjs, display/xauth from env); (b) GTK3/AT-SPI (mousepad); (c) Qt6/AT-SPI (FeatherPad, qBittorrent).

t5_blind_action.detail: (a) CDP: element box (page coords 420,396 126x47) + window.screenX/Y (10,10) + chromeTop (outerHeight-innerHeight=143) → screen (493,572) → xdotool click on the Xvfb display → page state IDLE→CLICKED read back through CDP. The one real subtlety is the coordinate-frame composition (page→window→screen), and it worked unmodified. (b) GTK/AT-SPI: right-click at text-node extents centre → popup published in-channel with real extents → blind-click 'Select All' → Text.getSelection [0,92] = whole buffer. (c) Qt/AT-SPI: FeatherPad 'File' menubar item extents → click → 12 menu items flip to SHOWING; qBittorrent 'Vitesse' tab extents → click → panel nodes appear. Every coordinate from the structured channel; every verification in the channel; zero screenshots in any decision loop.

measurements.notes: Closes the P2 item from DEEPENING-PLAN. The 2026-08-14 'blocked' was environmental (sandbox Chromium lifecycle), as suspected — the approach needed zero changes. Cross-stack note: the CDP path must COMPOSE three coordinate frames itself (page + window origin + chrome height, all read from the channel), while AT-SPI's DESKTOP_COORDS already answers in screen space — one call, no composition. For a desktop router that is an argument for taking geometry from the OS layer even when content comes from a browser-level channel; it is also exactly where the calibration rule from pages/click-dpr.html applies (never hardcode the frame transform, probe it).

runtime_verification.method: (a) CDP re-read of the page state element after the OS click; (b)(c) AT-SPI re-read of selection/menu/panel state after the click; screenshots kept as human evidence only.
runtime_verification.agreement: 4/4 blind clicks landed and produced their intended, channel-verified effect on the first attempt (CDP button, GTK context-menu item, Qt menubar item, Qt tab button).
